applicationTypes.name: Establish a new technical institution
applicationTypes.summary: For a promoter starting a new institution. Includes scrutiny, an expert visit and, if deficiencies remain, a hearing.

documents.name: Registered land deed or lease (min. 30 years)

applicationTypes.name: Extension of approval (self-disclosure)
applicationTypes.summary: Yearly renewal based on the institution's own disclosure of facilities. No scrutiny unless issues arise.

applicationTypes.name: Introduce or continue NRI seats
applicationTypes.summary: Up to 5% of approved intake for Non-Resident Indians.

applicationTypes.name: Increase in intake or additional course
applicationTypes.summary: More seats or a new course in an existing programme. Needs scrutiny and an expert visit.

applicationTypes.name: Start a new programme or level
applicationTypes.summary: A new programme (for example MCA) or level (for example PG) in an existing institution.

applicationTypes.name: Change of site or location
applicationTypes.summary: Moving the campus. Land, building and safety documents for the new site are checked, followed by an expert visit.

documents.name: Registered land deed or lease (min. 30 years)

applicationTypes.name: Convert diploma level to degree (or reverse)
applicationTypes.summary: Change of level for the whole institution.

applicationTypes.name: Merger of institutions
applicationTypes.summary: Two institutions under the same or different trusts, on the same campus or city, merge.

documents.name: Registered land deed or lease (min. 30 years)

applicationTypes.name: Extension of approval after a break
applicationTypes.summary: Restoring approval or intake after a gap year or punitive action.

applicationTypes.name: Supernumerary seats (FN/OCI/CIWG)
applicationTypes.summary: 15% seats over approved intake for foreign nationals, OCI and children of Indian workers in Gulf countries.

applicationTypes.name: Integrated or dual degree course
applicationTypes.summary: Introduce an integrated or dual degree.

applicationTypes.name: Fellow Programme in Management
applicationTypes.summary: Doctoral-level programme in management.

applicationTypes.name: Collaboration and twinning programme
applicationTypes.summary: Programmes with a foreign or Indian partner institution.

applicationTypes.name: Change course name, merge courses or reduce intake
applicationTypes.summary: Administrative change to courses. Scrutiny only.

applicationTypes.name: Change of institution name, university or type
applicationTypes.summary: Rename the institution or change its affiliating body. Scrutiny only.

applicationTypes.name: Women's institution to co-ed (or reverse)
applicationTypes.summary: Change in admission policy by gender.

applicationTypes.name: Closure of programmes or courses
applicationTypes.summary: Close a course progressively. Scrutiny only.

applicationTypes.name: Closure of the institution
applicationTypes.summary: Close the whole institution. Student and staff liabilities are checked.

applicationTypes.name: Change in bank details
applicationTypes.summary: Update the institution's bank account on record.

documents.name: Bank account details and cancelled cheque

applicationTypes.name: Change in name of Trust/Society/Company
applicationTypes.summary: Rename the promoting body.

applicationTypes.name: Conversion into a deemed-to-be university
applicationTypes.summary: Institution converts to deemed-university status.

applicationTypes.summary: Online or open and distance learning courses, processed twice a year.

glossary.full: All India Council for Technical Education
glossary.meaning: The national body that approves technical institutions and courses such as engineering, management, pharmacy and architecture.
The rulebook that says what each kind of request needs, who checks it and by when.
The yearly renewal that lets an existing institution keep running its approved courses.
The letter that grants approval for a new institution or a new course.
A letter listing the shortfalls found. The institution can fix them, appear before the hearing committee or appeal.
A letter refusing the request, always with written reasons.
Experts who inspect an institution, in person, online or both, when the handbook requires a visit.
The committee that hears an institution that still has shortfalls, before a decision is taken.
AICTE’s decision-making committee. It takes the final decision on every application.
The committee that hears an appeal against a decision. One appeal is allowed, within 7 days.
A letter from the State Government or the affiliating university saying it has no objection to the request.
An electronic signature. Every uploaded document must be signed by the Chairman or Secretary of the Trust or Society.
An online check of the submitted documents by the scrutiny committee.
A second check that looks only at the shortfalls already raised, nothing new.
A shortfall against the norms found during scrutiny or a visit, such as a missing document or too few faculty.
The number of student seats approved for a course.
A formal promise by the institution to meet a condition by a set date, such as submitting a renewed certificate.
How many years of land lease are left after allowing for the longest course. Renewal is blocked once it reaches zero.
A deadline timer that pauses while a file waits on the institution and runs only for the official who holds it.
A record of every action in which each entry is locked to the one before it, so any later edit is detectable.
A 64-character code calculated from a file. Change even one letter of the file and the code changes completely.
A random number published every 30 seconds by independent organisations worldwide. ANUMATI uses it to pick expert panels so nobody can rig the draw.
Fixed example cases that the rules must always get right. A rule change that breaks one cannot go live.
A decision that states its reasons in writing, so the institution knows exactly why.
One of the 10 AICTE offices that handle applications from the states in their region.
The legal body that sets up and runs a private institution. Its Chairman or Secretary signs the documents.
Government services that issue and confirm documents at the source, so a certificate can be checked without a paper copy.
For some requests the institution declares the facts and AICTE verifies them later, instead of a full check first.
Ending an institution or course. Progressive closure stops new admissions while current students finish.
The time limit for one stage of processing. Missing it raises an alert and then an escalation.
